title: Installation identity and isolated preview logins
outcome: Implement the observable behavior in tasks/VF-014.md while preserving real installation data.
acceptance: Read and satisfy the complete English specification in tasks/VF-014.md; its boundaries and negative criteria are mandatory.

AC-1 / Open a persistent installation and a disposable preview / Login and shell clearly distinguish their configured identities and data lifetime; only the preview warns that its accounts/history will be removed / Built browser test and owner guide

AC-2 / Log into two stacks on different localhost ports in one browser context, then reload and log out of either / Both remain logged in before logout; only the chosen stack loses authentication; no token is accepted by the other stack / Real HTTP/Chromium regression, not only route mocks
AC-3 / Repeat AC-2 using two 127.0.0.1 origins / Cookie lookup, login and logout remain coherent and isolated / Parameterized automated regression

AC-4 / Existing persistent installation uses the default cookie setting / Existing valid vf_session login remains usable; choosing a custom name changes login/read/logout coherently without rewriting account data / Authentication integration regression

AC-5 / Configure distinct cookie names on two persistent origins / Login isolation works without requiring disposable mode; helper-generated previews receive unique names automatically / Authentication and helper tests

AC-6 / Supply invalid identity/mode metadata or request identity anonymously / Invalid settings fail clearly; public metadata contains only intended labels/lifetime, never database URLs, provider secrets or filesystem paths / Settings/API unit tests

AC-7 / Finish a disposable test / Only its uniquely allocated test resources are removed; persistent installation resources are never selected / Helper boundary assertions and recorded cleanup evidence

Use only synthetic disposable data. No home SSH, real .env, provider calls, paid fallback, merge, deployment or automatic owner acceptance. Delegate only bounded subtasks when useful; no two writers in one checkout.
